description: The bar chart illustrates a comparative analysis of two model variants—“70B llama” and “8B llama”—across three distinct domains: “Health and Nutrition,” “Logistics,” and “Personal Finance.” Each domain is represented by a pair of stacked vertical bars, with the lower segment in teal representing “MVS” (Model Variance Score) and the upper segment in blue representing “1-MVS,” indicating the complementary portion of the total variance. The y-axis is scaled from 0.0 to 1.0, suggesting normalized values, likely representing proportions or normalized scores. In “Health and Nutrition,” the 70B llama model shows an MVS of approximately 0.6, while the 8B llama model has an MVS of about 0.4. In “Logistics,” both models exhibit similar MVS values around 0.5. In “Personal Finance,” the 70B llama model achieves an MVS of approximately 0.73, significantly higher than the 8B llama’s MVS of about 0.37. The consistent use of color coding and stacking allows for direct visual comparison of the contribution of MVS to the total variance within each model and domain, with the 70B llama generally showing higher MVS values across domains, particularly in “Personal Finance.” The chart’s layout, with domain titles above each pair of bars and a shared legend at the bottom, facilitates cross-domain and cross-model interpretation within the context of variance decomposition in large language models as discussed in the referenced paper.
